'''Günther Wyschofsky''' (born 8 May 1929 in [[Bischofswerda]]) is a former politician and official in the [[German Democratic Republic]].<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenGW>{{cite web|url=http://bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363%3B-1424.html?ID=3913|author1= Helmut Müller-Enbergs|author-link= Helmut Müller-Enbergs|author2= Andreas Herbst|author2-link= Andreas Herbst (Historian)|title=Wyschofsky, Günther *8.5.1929 Leiter der Abteilung Grundstoffindustrie des ZK der SED, Minister für chemische Industrie|publisher= Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur: Biographische Datenbanken |language= German|accessdate= 3 March 2015}}</ref>   He became a member of the powerful [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany#Central Committee|Central Committee]] of the country's ruling Socialist Unity Party in 1964.<ref name=AxSpriGW>{{Cite book |title=Es gab keine Macht gegen die Macht: Zusammenfassung|author=Günther Wyschofsky (as interviewee)|publisher=Springer-Verlag GmbH, Heidelberg |isbn=978-3-322-97052-7 |pages=189–211|date=1995|doi=10.1007/978-3-322-97052-7_8|chapter = Es gab keine Macht gegen die Macht}}</ref>     For more than two decades he also served as junior Minister for the Chemicals Industry.<ref name=ChemiedeGW>{{cite web|url=http://www.chemie.de/lexikon/G%C3%BCnther_Wyschofsky.html|title=Günther Wyschofsky|author=|publisher=CHEMIE.DE Information Service GmbH|date=|accessdate=3 March 2015}}</ref>

==Life==
Günther Wyschofsky was born in [[Bischofswerda]], a small industrial town in [[Upper Lusatia]] in then southern part of what was then Central Germany, and some 20&nbsp;km (12 miles) from the frontier with the republic of [[Czechoslovakia]], established slightly more than a decade before his birth. His father was a [[baker]] and [[Confectionery|confectioner]] who lost his job during the economic crisis of the 1920s and had joined the [[Communist Party of Germany|Communist Party]] (KPD) before 1933.<ref name=AxSpriGW/>   His mother worked as a glass maker.<ref name=AxSpriGW/>

He left school aged 14, at the height of the [[Second World War|war]], and undertook a training as a laboratory technician and pharmacist, after which he used his training professionally, working in [[Bischofswerda]] and nearby in [[Bautzen]].<ref name=AxSpriGW/>   The war ended in May 1945 which put an end to [[One-party state|one-]][[NSDAP|Party]] government. Wyschofsky joined the Communist Party. The next year, in April 1946 the [[Merger of the KPD and SPD into the Socialist Unity Party of Germany|contentious merger]] between the old Communist Party and the Moderate-left [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|SPD]] created the precondition for a return to [[One-party state|one-]][[Socialist Unity Party of Germany|party]] rule, this time under [[Soviet Military Administration in Germany|Soviet administration]] across the whole of what was now the [[Soviet occupation zone of Germany|Soviet occupation zone]] in what remained of Germany. Wyschofsky was one of thousands of former Communists who now lost no time in signing their membership over to the new [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany|Socialist Unity Party]] (''Sozialistische Einheitspartei Deutschlands'', SED). Between 1946 and 1948 he pursued his studies at the Workers' and Farmers' Faculty (ABF / ''{{lang|de|Arbeiter-und-Bauern-Fakultät}}'') in [[Halle (Saale)|Halle]]. Next he studied [[Chemistry]] at the [[TU Dresden|Dresden University of Technology]] and at the [[Leipzig University|Karl-Marx University]] (as it was then known) in [[Leipzig]], obtaining his degree in 1951.<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenGW/>

He then worked as an industrial chemist, till 1953 heading up the research laboratories at [[Volkseigener Betrieb|VEB]] Plastics in [[Espenhain]] which was then at the heart of a vast "[[Lignite|brown coal]]" mining area. Between 1953 and 1957 he worked for the [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany#Central Committee|Party Central Committee]] at a national level as an instructor and section leader in the Chemistry division of its [[Departments of the SED Central Committee#Basic Industries|Basic Industries Department]].<ref name=AxSpriGW/>

At this stage he was selected for a year of study at the [[Parteihochschule Karl Marx|Karl Marx Party Academy]], after which in 1958 he returned to working as an official of the Party Central Committee, now as deputy department head for Mining, Coal, Energy and Chemistry.  In 1959 he was promoted to the Headship of the [[Departments of the SED Central Committee#Basic Industries|Basic Industries Department]] for the Party Central Committee. That job lasted to 1962 when he was again promoted, now becoming Deputy President and Head of the Chemistry Planning department of the [[:de:Staatliche Plankommission|State Planning Commission]]. In May 1966 Wyschofsky was appointed Minister for the Chemicals Industry in succession to {{Interlanguage link|Siegbert Löschau|de}} who fell out of favour that year on account of his "inappropriate behaviour".<ref>''"....wegen unwürdigen Verhaltens".''</ref><ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenSL>{{cite web|url=http://bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363%3B-1424.html?ID=2149|author1= Andreas Herbst|author-link= Andreas Herbst (Historian)|title=Löschau, Siegbert *13.12.1929 Minister für chemische Industrie |publisher= Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur: Biographische Datenbanken |language= German|accessdate= 3 March 2015}}</ref>  Wyschofsky himself retained this ministerial post for more than twenty years, till [[Die Wende|November 1989]]<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenGW/> and the resignation of the [[:de:Ministerrat der DDR (1986–1989)|Stoph government]].<ref name=AxSpriGW/>

The [[Constitution of East Germany|constitution]] of the country was closely modeled on that of the [[Soviet Union]], and insisted on the leading role of The Party. Government Ministers held their posts at the pleasure of The Party and their job was to carry out The Party Central Committee decisions. Potential tensions arising from this situation were reduced by the fact that many ministers were also members of the [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany#Central Committee|Party Central Committee]]. Günther Wyschofsky was listed as a candidate for membership in January 1963, and after a wait of less than two years was elected one of the approximately 121 members of the Central Committee in December 1964.<ref>[[Neues Deutschland]] 6 December 1964</ref>   Later he was also Chairman, for the East German side, in the bilateral Economic Committees of the German Democratic Republic with [[Iran]] and with [[China]].<ref>Neues Deutschland 9 July 1989</ref>

Wyschofsky period in office saw the construction or massive expansion of several major industrial facilities that nearly half a century later are still important facilities in their respective sectors. These include the vast [[:de:PCK Raffinerie|Petro-chemicals facility]] in [[Schwedt]], the second refinery at [[Leuna]] and the extended adhesives plant at [[:de:Piesteritz|Piesteritz]]. On the other hand there were other less prestigious Chemicals plants which were left to deteriorate because the larger high-profile "beacon" facilities absorbed all the available investment capital.  He often found himself torn between insights deriving from his own expertise and the strictures of party discipline. With Wyschofsky it was always party discipline that won.
{{Quote box|bgcolor=#c6dbf7|align=right|width=41%|
:::'''Publication'''
In 2004 Günther Wyschofsky published a book entitled "Questions to a Contemporary witness" (''"Fragen an einen Zeitzeugen"''), derived from his day to day experiences in government.  It dealt with the political context for the political and economic problems of the former [[German Democratic Republic]].<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenGW/>}}
1990, the year of [[German reunification]], was also the year in which Günther Wyschofsky took early retirement. He returned to live in [[Bischofswerda]].<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenGW/>

*1970 [[Patriotic Order of Merit]] in Silver
*1974 [[Distinguished Service Medal of the National People's Army]]
*1977 [[:de:Verdienter Chemiearbeiter der Deutschen Demokratischen Republik|Honoured Chemical Worker]]
*1979 [[Patriotic Order of Merit]] in Gold
*1984 [[Patriotic Order of Merit]] Gold clasp
*1984 [[Honorary degree|Honorary doctorate]] of the [[:de:Technische Hochschule Leuna-Merseburg|"Carl Schorlemmer" Technical Academy]] ([[Leuna|Leuna-Merseburg]])
*1989 [[Order of Karl Marx]]
